title: Microsoft Purview: adaptive scope lifecycle status controls for recipients and site owners (GCC, GCC High and DoD)
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, existing scope controls and retention licensing are supported, and the planned lifecycle control remains undocumented. One minor correction is needed because the checklist asks readers to review role assignments without a corresponding controls-table row.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans explicit lifecycle-state evaluation control for recipients and site owners in Purview adaptive scopes.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Adaptive Scopes will provide administrators with explicit control over lifecycle-state evaluation for recipients and site owners

claims.claim: The planned control is intended to align policy targeting and scope membership with organisational requirements.
claims.quote: helping ensure policy targeting and scope membership remain aligned with organizational requirements.

claims.claim: An adaptive scope uses a query to define changing membership of users, Microsoft 365 groups or sites.
claims.quote: An adaptive scope uses a query that you specify, so you can define the membership of users or groups included in that query. ... There are three different types of adaptive scopes

claims.claim: Communication compliance, retention and auto-labeling policies can target adaptive scopes.
claims.quote: When you create a communication compliance policy, a policy for retention, or an auto-labeling policy, you can add an adaptive scope for your policy.

claims.claim: Communication compliance policies do not support SharePoint sites or OneDrive accounts in adaptive scopes.
claims.quote: For communication compliance policies: - SharePoint sites and OneDrive accounts aren't supported.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the new control's default state or what happens on arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview adaptive scope lifecycle status control licensing prerequisites rollout default; read roadmap, Adaptive scopes, New-AdaptiveScope and Set-AdaptiveScope. None states the planned control's default.

claims.where: controls[0].ui and controls[0].api; summary; What's changing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no UI setting or command for the planned recipient and site owner lifecycle evaluation control.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview adaptive scopes lifecycle evaluation recipient site owner status control; adaptive scopes recipient site owner lifecycle evaluation control PowerShell Set-AdaptiveScope. Read Adaptive scopes and New/Set-AdaptiveScope; no dedicated lifecycle setting found.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not described which lifecycle states the new control evaluates or their policy outcomes.
claims.quote: Searched: adaptive scopes recipient site owner lifecycle evaluation control default lifecycle states; read roadmap, Adaptive scopes, New-AdaptiveScope and Set-AdaptiveScope. No states or outcomes for the new control are specified.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap and Learn do not explain how the new control maps to Users, SharePoint sites and Microsoft 365 Groups scopes.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview adaptive scopes recipient site owner lifecycle evaluation control. Read roadmap and Adaptive scopes, including the three scope types; no mapping of the planned lifecycle control to these types is given.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not said whether the new control follows existing scope evaluation timing.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview adaptive scope lifecycle status control prerequisites rollout default; read roadmap and Adaptive scopes. Existing daily evaluation and five-day propagation are documented, but timing for the planned control is not.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The role that will manage the new lifecycle control is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview adaptive scope lifecycle status control prerequisites; read roadmap, Adaptive scopes, New-AdaptiveScope and Set-AdaptiveScope. Existing scope permissions are documented; no permission specific to the new control is given.

claims.claim: Rollout mechanics and prerequisites specific to the new control are not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Purview adaptive scope lifecycle status control licensing prerequisites rollout default; read roadmap and Adaptive scopes. No rollout procedure or prerequisites for the planned lifecycle control are specified.

claims.claim: No source says that existing scopes change when the new control arrives.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview adaptive scope lifecycle status control rollout default; read roadmap and Adaptive scopes. Neither states that existing scopes change on arrival; the briefing's preparation is advice rather than a guaranteed unchanged default.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes no new identity or permission model.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Adaptive Scopes will provide administrators with explicit control over lifecycle-state evaluation for recipients and site owners, helping ensure policy targeting and scope membership remain aligned with organizational requirements.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The roadmap describes an administrator control, not autonomous behaviour or a change for end users.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Adaptive Scopes will provide administrators with explicit control over lifecycle-state evaluation for recipients and site owners

claims.where: controls[1].note; What's changing; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The advanced query builder uses IsInactiveMailbox to exclude inactive mailboxes or target just inactive mailboxes.
claims.quote: You must use the advanced query builder if you want to exclude inactive mailboxes. Or conversely, target just inactive mailboxes. For this configuration, use the OPATH property IsInactiveMailbox

claims.claim: Users without a valid licence for adaptive scopes do not have the policy settings applied to them.
claims.quote: it might be because it includes users who don't have a valid license for adaptive scopes. These users don't have the policy settings applied to them.

claims.claim: Existing adaptive scope queries run daily.
claims.quote: These dynamic queries run daily against the attributes or properties that you specify for the selected scope.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Existing scope queries can take up to five days to fully populate, and Microsoft advises waiting before adding a newly created scope to a policy.
claims.quote: It can take up to five days for the queries to fully populate and changes aren't immediate. Factor in this delay by waiting a few days before you add a newly created scope to a policy.

claims.claim: The scope member details list can take up to five days to reflect added or removed members.
claims.quote: It might take up to five days for the member details list to update added or removed members.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Scope details displays Added for current members and Removed for members who no longer match the query.
claims.quote: Review the State column in the list that shows Added for members within the adaptive scope or Removed if the member was previously in the adaptive scope but removed now they no longer match the scope query.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Creating an adaptive scope requires a role group with Scope Manager.
claims.quote: Any role group with the Scope Manager role can create an adaptive scope.

claims.claim: Scope Manager is included in the six built-in role groups listed in the briefing.
claims.quote: The Scope Manger role is included in the following built-in role groups: - Compliance Administrator - Compliance Data Administrator - Organization Management - Records Management - Communication Compliance - Communication Compliance Admins

claims.claim: Keep Full directory when not restricting a scope by administrative unit.
claims.quote: If you don't want to restrict the adaptive scope by using administrative units, or your organization hasn't configured administrative units, keep the default of Full directory.

claims.claim: Scope queries can be created through Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes > + Create scope > administrative unit > scope type > Advanced query builder.
claims.quote: Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes. ... select + Create scope. ... first asked to assign an administrative unit. ... Select the type of scope ... Alternatively, you can select Advanced query builder

claims.claim: New-AdaptiveScope -Name <String> -LocationType User -RawQuery <String> creates a user adaptive scope with an advanced query.
claims.quote: New-AdaptiveScope -Name <String> -LocationType <DynamicBoundaryLocationType> -RawQuery <String> ... Valid values are: - User ... The RawQuery parameter switches the scope to advanced query mode.

claims.claim: Membership is reached through Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes > scope > Details > Scope details.
claims.quote: Select Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes. ... Select an existing adaptive scope from the list. ... From the Details flyout pane, select Scope details.

claims.claim: Get-AdaptiveScopeMembers -Identity <scope name> -State Removed retrieves former scope members.
claims.quote: Get-AdaptiveScopeMembers -Identity "US Finance Users" -State Removed ... This example retrieves the past members of the adaptive scope US Finance Users.
